_comment: A broken deep cavalry block rounds a hill in its line of flight with no man held against it. Team 1's 80 horses (default Cavalry geometry: 9 files by 9 ranks, about 320 wu wide and 960 wu deep) spawn ALREADY routing (starting_state 3, morale 1.0) facing south, their own back edge, with their front rank 220 wu short of a hill (block terrain, x 780-1040, y 1400-1600) that stands across the eastern half of the block; the block's centre line (x 820) passes 40 wu inside the hill's west face. The flight rounds the hill by its west end with the block's own half-width as its margin, its heading turning onto the detour at a bounded rate so the slot grid never swings off the men, and any man whose run would still carry him onto the hill veers along its face. Before the fix the flight cleared only the anchor's own margin (a body radius plus 18 wu): the eastern files ran into the hill's north face and were held there. Measured with full state dumps at the declared ticks (soldiers_at_block_terrain_edge counts men within a body radius plus 1 wu of the hill): with the fix, 0 men at the hill at every sampled tick, mean body-to-slot gap at most 27.7 wu and at most 1 man more than 100 wu off his slot; before the fix 3 men at the hill at tick 240, 7 at 300, 11 at 330 and 10 at 350, a mean gap of 46.3 wu and 8 men more than 100 wu off their slots at tick 350. The anchor is at about (737, 939) at tick 240 and (645, 1153) at tick 330; before the fix (796.8, 932.5) and (773.1, 1144.2). The tick-8 position pins are setup pins (the spawn, so a re-spaced spawn fails loudly), not claims about the fix. A routing unit's rout timer (6 s) runs out at tick 360 and it rallies; the clip ends at tick 352, just before that, so it shows only the flight. A small idle team-0 squadron 600 wu east keeps the router in the close sim tier (an isolated block drops to the far tier, which has no bodies); all_teams_control leaves both sides without AI, so neither moves on its own. Flat declared map apart from the hill; drill mode. Driven live through the real SelectionManager by tools/demo/DemoInputRecorder.gd; world coordinates; physics ticks (60/s).
